references.text: Joseph's proposal to Pharaoh to appoint a wise man and overseer to gather food during the seven good years.
The purpose of the food collection: that the food should serve as a reserve for the land during the seven years of famine.
The actual implementation of the plan: Joseph gathered grain in enormous quantities during the seven good years.
The result of the food collection: Joseph supplied Egypt and surrounding nations with food during the famine.
The ant that gathers food in summer as preparation - a parallel to the wisdom of storing reserves in good times.
The prophecy of a great famine and the church's response by gathering aid, emphasizing the importance of preparation.
Complementary parts of Joseph's plan in Egypt: first storage of surplus (41:35), then distribution during the famine (47:24).
Theological parallel: God's instruction to store food to save lives during an upcoming catastrophe (the flood versus the famine).
Direct narrative connection: 41:35 is the plan for storage, and 41:48 is the implementation of that same plan.
